<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/monitoring-plugin/pull/873):

>## Summary
>
>Adds Cypress performance benchmarks that measure wall-clock render times for key Incidents page operations under escalating data loads, serving as regression indicators for future code changes.
>
>### New test specs
>
>- **`01.performance_benchmark.cy.ts`** — Measures initial chart render times:
>  - Incidents chart with 100 / 200 / 500 alerts (single incident)
>  - Alerts detail chart after incident selection (100 / 200 / 500 alerts)
>  - Multi-incident chart (20 uniform incidents)
>  - Mixed-size incidents chart (12 heterogeneous incidents, 67 alerts)
>
>- **`02.performance_walkthrough.cy.ts`** — Measures incremental re-render cost during interactive use:
>  - Severity filter apply/clear cycles
>  - Time range switching (1d → 3d → 7d → 15d → 1d)
>  - Table row expansion with 100 and 500 alerts
>
>### New fixtures
>
>- `22-benchmark-20-incidents.yaml` — 20 uniform single-alert incidents
>- `23-benchmark-mixed-size-incidents.yaml` — 12 incidents with 1–15 alerts each
>
>### Threshold calibration
>
>Thresholds were calibrated across **6 runs on 2 different CI clusters** and set at **1.5x+ the worst observed value**, rounded to a single significant digit. The Incidents page rendering is not on the critical performance path of the overall system, so the thresholds are intentionally generous — the goal is to catch significant regressions, not to enforce tight performance budgets.
>
>### Other changes
>
>- Documentation: `docs/incident_detection/tests/performance/overview.md` and `03.endurance_test_source.md`
